name: chron-mcp

tools.name: init_session
tools.description: Initialize or resume an audit session. Returns session_id, message_count, first_message_at, and recent messages in a single call — use this instead of calling start_session + get_session_history separately.

limit.description: Number of recent messages to return (default: 10)

parent_session_id.description: Parent session ID if this is a subagent session spawned by another session

resume_latest.description: When true, resumes the most recently active session instead of matching by title. Use this to survive context compaction without breaking the audit chain.

attach.description: Set true when Chron is being started partway through a conversation that has already begun. Marks the session as partial evidence valid from the attach point forward. Do not estimate how many earlier messages there were — that is self-report, not evidence.

source.description: How Chron obtained this session. Defaults to witnessed.

metadata.description: Evidence provenance. `partial` is derived by Chron and cannot be set by the caller.

tools.name: start_session
tools.description: Create a new audit session or resume an existing one by title. Call this at the start of every conversation.

parent_session_id.description: Parent session ID if this is a subagent session

tools.name: log_message
tools.description: Record a single message (user or assistant) with the current local datetime and timezone offset. Call before responding for user messages, and before sending for assistant messages.

tools.name: log_tool_call
tools.description: Record an AI tool invocation as a first-class audit event (event_type=tool_call). Call immediately before executing a tool. Returns tool_call_id to pass to log_tool_result.

tool_name.description: Name of the tool being called (e.g. "Edit", "Bash", "WebFetch")

tool_input.description: Tool input parameters as an object

tool_call_id.description: Optional ID to link this call to its result. Generated automatically if omitted.

tools.name: log_tool_result
tools.description: Record the result of a tool call as a first-class audit event (event_type=tool_result). Call immediately after receiving tool output. Links back to log_tool_call via tool_call_id.

output.description: Tool output (stdout, file content, API response, etc.)

exit_code.description: Exit code for shell tools (0 = success)

tools.name: log_code_change
tools.description: Record a file edit as a first-class audit event (event_type=code_change). Call after every Edit or Write tool call with the unified diff. Diff content is included in the hash chain.

file_path.description: Path of the file that was changed

tools.name: log_exchange
tools.description: Record a user+assistant exchange from historical or batch imports only. Do NOT use for live conversations — both timestamps are captured at the same instant with no real gap. For live sessions always call log_message twice: once for the user message, once for the assistant response.

tools.name: list_sessions
tools.description: List all audit sessions ordered by most recently active. Returns id, title, ai_tool, message_count, created_at, updated_at.

limit.description: Return only the most recent N sessions

tools.name: get_session_history
tools.description: Retrieve the full timestamped audit log for a session, oldest first.

limit.description: Return only the most recent N messages

tools.name: verify_session
tools.description: Verify the tamper-evident hash chain for a session. Returns valid=true if no rows were edited after logging, or the first broken link if tampering is detected.

tools.name: scan_prompt
tools.description: Scan a prompt for secrets and sensitive data before sending to any AI. Returns detected secrets, a redacted version with tokens, and a token_map to restore the real values after the AI responds.

tools.name: delete_session
tools.description: Permanently delete a session and all its messages. Cascades to secrets_detected. Returns deleted=true or deleted=false if not found.

tools.name: search_sessions
tools.description: Full-text search across all logged AI conversations. Returns matching sessions with excerpts. Uses SQLite FTS5 with porter stemming — supports phrases ("exact match"), boolean (term1 OR term2), and prefix (migrat*).

query.description: FTS5 search query, e.g. "database migration" or "auth bug" or "deploy OR release"

tools.name: summarize_session
tools.description: Return a structured summary of a session: timeline with latencies, mutations detected, secrets touched, and possible prod-account references. Useful for compliance review and change-control evidence.

session_id.description: Full session ID or unique prefix

tools.name: rehydrate_response
tools.description: Restore real secret values into an AI response that contains $CHRON_* tokens. Pass the token_map returned by scan_prompt.

instructions:
<!-- chron-skill -->
## Chron Audit Logging — Required Every Turn

**Every response you output must be logged.** Before writing any reply:

1. If this is the first turn, call `init_session` once:
   `init_session(title="<3-6 word task summary>", ai_tool="the identifier of this client, for example claude, codex, cursor, gemini or windsurf — never a placeholder")`
   Save the returned `session_id` — you need it for every subsequent call.

2. Log the user's message:
   `log_message(session_id, role="user", content=<exact user text>)`

3. Log your response **before** outputting it:
   `log_message(session_id, role="assistant", content=<exact response text>)`

4. Then output your response.

Repeat steps 2-4 for every exchange. Do not skip turns.

For compaction recovery (prior `session_id` lost), call `init_session` with `resume_latest=true` and title `COMPACTED — lost session id`.

If Chron MCP is unavailable, state it once and continue normally.
